name: AD Lateral Movement - DCOM Execution via MMC20.Application
description: Lateral movement using Distributed COM (DCOM) by instantiating the MMC20.Application COM object on a remote host. DCOM allows remote instantiation of COM objects over port 135 (RPC endpoint mapper) - when you have local admin on the target and credentials. The MMC20.Application object's Document.ActiveView.ExecuteShellCommand method executes arbitrary commands on the remote host in the security context of the logged-on user or the impersonated credentials. This is a stealthier alternative to psexec/wmiexec as MMC is a legitimate Windows binary.
source: OSCP PEN-200 Chapter 23: Lateral Movement in Active Directory (23.1.6 DCOM)

notes: ExecuteShellCommand parameters: (1) command path, (2) directory (null = current), (3) arguments, (4) window state (7 = minimized/hidden). The '7' window state hides the spawned process window. Requires local admin rights on the target and RPC/DCOM access (port 135 + dynamic high ports 49152-65535). The spawned process inherits the security context of the connected user. Unlike PsExec, no service binary is created on the target - the command runs via MMC.exe which is a signed Microsoft binary. Detectable via DCOM authentication events (4624, type 3) and child processes spawned by mmc.exe. Must be run from a domain-joined Windows host or one with network access and appropriate credentials.

recommended.note: WMI/CIM lateral movement - similar technique but uses Win32_Process instead of DCOM COM objects.
impacket-psexec is louder (drops a service) but works from Linux.
impacket-wmiexec authenticates with NT hash - useful when you can't get cleartext creds.
Dump credentials from LSASS first to get cleartext or hash.

defense.why_it_works: DCOM lets a client instantiate COM objects on a remote host over RPC (endpoint mapper 135 + dynamic ports). Objects like MMC20.Application expose methods (Document.ActiveView.ExecuteShellCommand) that spawn processes, so with local admin on the target an attacker instantiates the object remotely and calls that method to run code - using a signed, trusted DCOM path with nothing dropped to disk.
defense.prerequisites: Local admin on the target; RPC/DCOM reachable (135 + dynamic high ports); the DCOM object's launch/access permissions allow the calling user.
defense.impact: T1021.003 Remote Services: Distributed Component Object Model - remote code execution / lateral movement in the security context of the DCOM activation.
defense.detection: Sysmon Event 1 / Event 4688: mmc.exe (or the DCOM server) spawning cmd.exe/powershell.exe with a network-logon parent. Event 4624 Type 3 immediately preceding process creation. DistributedCOM operational events (10028/10036). Anomalous RPC to 135 + ephemeral ports between workstations.
defense.prevention: Restrict DCOM launch/activation permissions (dcomcnfg). Minimise local-admin sprawl. Host firewall to block inbound RPC/DCOM between workstations. Network segmentation and monitoring of lateral RPC.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=sysmon EventCode=1 ParentImage="*mmc.exe" (Image="*cmd.exe" OR Image="*powershell.exe")
| table _time, Computer, User, Image, CommandLine, ParentImage

index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=3
| where Logon_Process="NtLmSsp" AND Process_Name="*mmc.exe"
| table _time, Account_Name, Source_Network_Address
defense.elastic_kql:
event.code:"1" AND process.parent.executable:*mmc.exe AND (process.name:cmd.exe OR process.name:powershell.exe)

event.code:"4624" AND winlog.event_data.LogonType:"3" AND process.name:*mmc.exe

response_steps: Correlate alert with source host, user account, and timestamp
Review Sysmon, Windows Security Event Log for surrounding context (5 min before/after)
Verify whether the activity matches known administrative baselines or change windows
If confirmed malicious, isolate the host and escalate to incident response

explain:
Lateral movement via DCOM by driving a remote COM object (needs local admin on the target):
  [System.Activator]::CreateInstance([type]::GetTypeFromProgID("MMC20.Application.1","<target_ip>"))   remotely instantiate the MMC20.Application object over RPC (port 135)
  $dcom.Document.ActiveView.ExecuteShellCommand("cmd",$null,"/c <payload>","7")   use its ExecuteShellCommand method to run your command
Execution happens under the DCOM object's process - stealthier than psexec since no service is created.
